rationale: Verbal root recurring in this kephalaion (lines 6, 9, 14, 23) characterizing the kind of word/act that constitutes ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin' (line 15) and harms the cross of light. Always functions in opposition to righteous speech. Forms agentive ⲣⲉϩⲱⲱⲃⲉ/ⲣⲉϥⲱⲱⲃⲉ 'transgressor' parallel to ⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sinner.' Etymology uncertain but semantic field is clearly transgression/breach. Lycopolitan.

Technical phrase organizing this kephalaion: the speech-act that constitutes sin against the cross of light. Catalogued in lines 9-14 as encompassing words about killing (men/cattle/trees), envious speech (eye/wrath/gall), envy (φθόνος), accusation/slander against brothers. Distinguished from righteous words about mercy and the soul's release.

Possibly reduplicated form related to ϩⲱϣ 'press, oppress' or to ϩⲱϣⲉ 'reckon, weary.' Context (paired with ϩⲓⲥⲉ 'toil' and modifying 'the bones') supports a noun for physical exhaustion or the breaking-down of bodily structure under labor. Confidence low.

proposed_english: the word of the (evil) eye / envious word
rationale: Literally 'word of eye' — the eye in Coptic moral vocabulary names jealousy/envy (cf. ⲃⲁⲗ ⲙⲡⲟⲛⲏⲣⲟⲥ 'evil eye' tradition). Listed in this page's catalogue alongside φθόνος as a sub-type of transgressing speech. Distinguished here from φθόνος itself by being collocated with bitterness/gall (the bodily humors of jealousy).

proposed_english: to plot against / to scheme against (tentative)
rationale: Verbal idiom in line 14 'one shall ⲛⲁⲥⲁⲣϥ ⲥⲁ his brother' as the defining action of the accusation-word. Possibly future ⲛⲁ- + ⲥⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'destroy, demolish' (with 3sg.m suffix). Captures the hostile-speech sense required by context. Confidence low.

Possibly compound ⲡⲱⲣⲡ̄ ('first' = ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄) + ϩⲁⲧⲉ ('front, before' = ϩⲏ). Functions in line 7 as a discourse-marker linking back to a topic addressed before. Could alternatively be a cosmic-correspondential epithet ('the foremost'). Confidence low.

Line 28 in the physician-simile: 'a ⲟⲩⲱⲃⲁ in his body' that the wounded man desires (presumably to remove). Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱⲃⲁ/ϩⲱⲡⲉ 'stripe, scourge mark' or related bodily-injury term. Fits medical-pathological context.

Line 30 in the physician-simile sequence: physician 'banishes the wound and ⲟⲩⲁⲭⲉϥ.' Possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲟⲩⲱⲱϫϥ̄ 'cleanse, scour' or related healing-action verb. Fits the surgical-cleansing register. Confidence low.

Line 32 in the iron-treatment sequence ϩⲙ̄ ⲡⲃⲁⲛⲓⲡⲉ 'in the iron.' Possibly reduplicated form of ⲱⲱⲧ 'kindle, set ablaze' or causative ⲁ-ⲱⲱⲧ-ⲥ̄ 'cause-her-to-burn.' Surgical cauterization sense fits the wise-physician simile.
